_meta.indication: Reduction of blood pressure when oral therapy is not feasible or not desirable

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel, placebo-controlled study in patients with preoperative hypertension scheduled for cardiac surgery
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with a history of hypertension or hypertensive pre-operatively (mean baseline SBP 179 mm Hg) undergoing CABG and/or valve replacement, with blood pressure to be lowered by at least 15%
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Treatment failure rate during the treatment period (bailout for lack of efficacy, safety, or failure to achieve at least 15% decrease in SBP)
pivotal_trials.result: Clevidipine superior to placebo: 43/52 responded on clevidipine versus 4/53 on placebo

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled study similar to ESCAPE-1 but in post-operative cardiac surgery patients
pivotal_trials.population: Post-operative cardiac surgery patients (CABG or valve surgery) within four hours of procedure with minimum SBP 140 mm Hg (mean SBP 148 mm Hg) requiring a 15% decrease in blood pressure
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Treatment failure (bailout for efficacy, safety, or failure to achieve at least a 15% decrease in SBP)
pivotal_trials.result: Substantially fewer clevidipine subjects required bailout: 5/61 clevidipine versus 39/49 placebo

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>2%) are headache, nausea, and vomiting. In the perioperative placebo-controlled studies atrial fibrillation (21% CLV vs 12% placebo in ESCAPE-2) and nausea (21% vs 12%) were common; hypotension and reflex tachycardia are potential consequences of rapid upward titration.
target_moa: Clevidipine is a dihydropyridine L-type calcium channel blocker; L-type calcium channels mediate the influx of calcium during depolarization in arterial smooth muscle, and clevidipine reduces mean arterial blood pressure by decreasing systemic vascular resistance

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee because the drug is not the first in its class, the clinical study design was acceptable, and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues

summary.text: Standard NDA submitted under section 505(b)(1), dated July 2, 2007, reviewed and approved first-cycle for reduction of blood pressure when oral therapy is not feasible or not desirable; the application was not referred to an advisory committee, with deferred pediatric studies required under PREA.
